source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 24 MW of IT capacity, ranking 17th among the 25 Virginia facilities that disclose power and amounting to 1.5 percent of the state's 1,603 MW of published load.

Virginia maps 330 data center facilities, and only 25 of them publish a power figure. Those 25 total 1,603 MW, so the state's disclosed capacity is a floor rather than a total. Sterling's 24 MW sits inside that small disclosing group, and its 154,230 square feet of technical space is the only other physical measure the operator publishes.

For AI specifically, power is the number that constrains accelerator density, because a hall can only host as many GPUs as it can feed and cool. A 24 MW campus is a substantial asset, but the published specification stops at capacity and floor area. It states no grid interconnect, no cooling design, and no certifications, so nothing in the record says whether dense GPU clusters could be hosted there.

The suitability score of 65 is derived only from published IT capacity and operator type, and it flags announced expansion as missing. That is the honest limit of the record. The data cannot say how much power Virginia's data centers actually draw, how much of it is contracted, or how much headroom the local grid has, because 305 of the 330 mapped facilities disclose nothing at all.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
